statement: MessageRouter shutdown retires one transport lifetime: late delivery cannot implicitly restart it; connecting and connected sockets, pending dials and reconnect callbacks retire with that lifetime; stale completions cannot repopulate retired state or affect a later explicitly initialized lifetime. Existing caller cancellation, correlated-response retirement, delivery classification and bounded shutdown remain one transport contract.

constraints.statement: Extend MessageRouter and its existing delivery cancellation/connection owners. Do not add a competing retry or request cancellation owner, consumer shutdown workaround, arbitrary sleep, timeout increase or error absorption.

Preserve explicit initialize after completed shutdown as a new lifetime. Initialization concurrent with shutdown must serialize or refuse; implicit delivery initialization is allowed only before the first shutdown. Captured old lifetime work never acquires new authority.

Own connecting sockets from allocation, terminate and settle pending connection work within the existing shutdown grace, reject late direct connect/adoption/delivery, and prevent retired reconnect completion or cleanup from modifying a new lifetime.

First reproduce the lifecycle defects with deterministic real-owner tests, then prove caller cancellation, retired late responses, queue/reconnect and shutdown interaction. No full release or live statistical run before focused proof and independent verification.

The release failure test places multiple logical nodes around process-global state. Repair that invalid multi-node fixture in a separately scoped Quest, not by cleanup reordering or weakening its assertion. This Quest changes only the router lifetime, its contract documentation, witnesses and generated metadata.
